column3: [tense] This garbage truck is about to hit your little brother. And he has no idea.
But today, you're a thousand times faster than everyone else. To you, that truck is crawling.
[quickly] So just grab him and run, right?
[nervous] Wrong. At your speed, your hands would hit him harder than the truck ever could.
So you do the hardest thing a fast person can do. [short pause] You go slow.
[strained] Every centimeter takes you a full minute. Your arms are shaking. Everything in you screams: hurry.
[tense] The truck is right there. Its brakes are smoking…
[whispers] Is he going to make it?
[panicked] You closed your eyes for one second. Now you're a hundred times faster.
And you take one single step toward your mom.
[shocked] That bang? That was you. One normal step, times a hundred, is faster than the speed of sound.
Every window in your house just blew out. And a thousand paper cranes are hanging in the air.
[sad] Your shoes are smoking. Your parents are covering their ears. Because of you.
[softly] So you go outside and sit on the curb. [short pause] And tomorrow, you'll be ten times faster again.
[wonder] It's raining. But the raindrops… aren't falling.
You're ten times faster than the rest of the world. So every drop just floats. You can walk right between them.
[softly] You catch one in your hand. It's the most beautiful thing you've ever seen.
So you call your best friend to tell him.
[softly] But his voice… is gone. Just a deep rumble, like thunder far away.
[whispers] And now nobody in the world can hear you anymore.
[excited] You knock over a glass of water. And you catch it. In mid-air.
Then you scoop the water back in.
Cornflakes fall like snow. You eat the whole box.
[laughs] Then you go for a little jog. Two hundred and fifty kilometers an hour.
You overtake a delivery van. On foot. The driver can't believe his eyes.
[proud] And the bus that always leaves without you? You wave at it as you pass.
[ominous] But this is only day two. Tomorrow you'll be ten times faster. And that's when it gets dangerous.
Your mom drops an egg. And you have time to walk around the table… and catch it.
You say: "Mom, it's me." But to her, you sound like a bird.
[sad] And for one second, she's scared of you. One second for her. Ten for you.
So you write on the whiteboard. Then she writes back. Her hand is shaking. Every letter takes forever.
[softly] She doesn't ask what happened. She doesn't ask what you are.
[softly] She asks if you're hurt.
[ominous] And this is only day two.
[tense] Every time you sleep, you wake up ten times faster. So every day is ten times shorter than the one before.
Twenty-four hours. Then two and a half. Then fifteen minutes.
[dread] And it all adds up to one moment. Nine o'clock this morning. The minute your little brother blows out his candles.
[whispers] You could live a thousand more days… and never get there.
[determined] Unless… you never fall asleep again.
[softly] This tear on your mom's cheek has been frozen in place… for seven days.
Because you're a million times faster than her. One of her seconds lasts twelve of your days.
[tense] And you keep getting faster. Ten million. A hundred million. One billion.
[wonder] And now you can see something no human has ever seen.
[whispers] Light… moving. Crawling across the table, slower than a turtle.
[softly] You place the last paper crane. That's one thousand. Enough for one wish.
[whispers] But you're so tired… [short pause] Can you stay awake?
